title: An ACA 1 mm survey of HzRGs in the ELAIS-S1: survey description and first results
question: Characterize the 1.3 mm continuum (thermal dust vs non-thermal synchrotron) and serendipitous molecular gas line properties of high-redshift radio galaxy (HzRG) candidates selected in the ELAIS-S1 field, and evaluate the efficiency of IR-radio selection criteria.

what.value: ATLAS 1.4 GHz and 2.3 GHz radio catalogues and photometry

evidence.loc: The choice of the ELAIS-S1 field
evidence.quote: The Australia Telescope Large Area Survey (ATLAS) covered the field at 1.4\,GHz (at 10$''$ $\times$ 7$''$ spatial resolution) and 2.3\,GHz (at 33$''$ $\times$ 20$''$ spatial resolution; (cite: norris06), (cite: middelberg08), (cite: zinn12), (cite: hales14), (cite: franzen15); Section [2.2](#sec:radphot))

evidence.loc: The choice of the ELAIS-S1 field
evidence.quote: Molonglo Observatory Synthesis Telescope (cite: mills81) observations in the same field provided 843\,MHz counterparts (at 62$''$ $\times$43$''$ spatial resolution) for about 10% of the 1.4 GHz catalogue (cite: randall12).

evidence.loc: The choice of the ELAIS-S1 field
evidence.quote: Finally, ELAIS-S1 is covered by the GaLactic and Extragalactic All-Sky MWA survey (GLEAM; (cite: wayth15), (cite: hurleyWalker17)) in the frequency range between 72 and 231 MHz

what.value: TGSS ADR 150 MHz radio survey catalogue

evidence.loc: The choice of the ELAIS-S1 field
evidence.quote: as well as the alternative data release of the TIFR GMRT Sky Survey (cite: intema17) at 150\,MHz (FWHM$\sim$25$''$ \,[^4]).

For 15 out of the 36 sources in the sample, shown in Tab. [\[tab:samp\]](#tab:samp), there are spectroscopic redshifts available from (cite: mao12) (indicated by M12 in Tab. [\[tab:samp\]](#tab:samp)) and (cite: vaccari15) (MVF).

Another 15 objects have photometric redshift estimates from (cite: rowanrobinson13) (RR13), the *Herschel* Extragalactic Legacy Project (cite: duncan18), the Dark Energy Survey (cite: hoyle18), and the photometric redshifts catalogue of the *Spitzer* Extragalactic Representative Volume Survey (cite: pforr19).

evidence.loc: The Sunyaev-Zel’dovich effect as a physical explanation
evidence.quote: We have checked in Atacama Cosmology Telescope (cite: Naess2020; Hilton2021) maps for evidence of large scale tSZE imprints on the CMB.

recipe.goal: Select HzRG candidate sample from multi-frequency radio and MIR catalogues
recipe.method: Cross-match ATLAS 2.3 GHz, MOST 843 MHz, and GMRT 610 MHz catalogues to ATLAS 1.4 GHz (M08) positions using 9'', 25'', and 6'' radii; cross-match 1.4 GHz positions with Spitzer SEIP MIR catalogue using 7'' radius; apply USS, LRS, and IFRS flux and colour cuts.
key_parameters: Matching radii: 9'' (2.3 GHz), 25'' (843 MHz), 6'' (610 MHz), 7'' (SEIP IR), 2'' (redshift catalogues)
assumptions: S_1.4GHz > 1 mJy ensures an AGN-like radio emitter (L_1.4GHz > 10^24.5 W Hz^-1) at z >= 1.5

recipe.goal: Measure 1.3 mm continuum fluxes and stack undetected sources
recipe.method: Fit elliptical Gaussian components to detections > 4.2 sigma and detections > 3 sigma matching an IRAC source using CASA imfit; stack continuum maps of 11 undetected sources at z > 0.8.
key_parameters: Central source matching radius <= 3.5''; field source IRAC matching radius <= 2''; SNR thresholds 4.2 sigma and 3 sigma
assumptions: Negative K-correction of thermal SEDs implies similar flux levels across z > 0.8 for thermal-dominated sources.

recipe.goal: Fit radio SEDs and extrapolate synchrotron contribution at 233 GHz
recipe.method: Match candidates with GLEAM (65'' radius) and TGSS (15'' radius); fit multi-frequency radio photometry (150 MHz to 2.3 GHz) with a single power law S_nu propto nu^alpha and extrapolate to 233 GHz to classify mm emission as synchrotron or thermal.
key_parameters: GLEAM 200 MHz-wide band (170-231 MHz); N = 100 bootstrap iterations; synchrotron-dominated threshold S^fit_233 > 0.5 * S^obs_233 within 1 sigma; thermal-dominated threshold S^fit_233 < 0.5 * S^obs_233 by > 3 sigma
assumptions: Single power law S_nu propto nu^alpha from radio to 233 GHz; for sources with <= 2 radio points, assumed median spectral index alpha = -0.68 with population deviation factor of 1.4.

recipe.goal: Search for serendipitous emission lines in ACA spectral cubes
recipe.method: Subtract continuum in the image plane, generate cubes at 20, 60, and 80 km/s resolution in tclean, and run SoFiA with spatial and spectral Gaussian smoothing kernels to identify emission lines.
key_parameters: Spatial Gaussian kernels: 3, 6, 9''; spectral kernels: 60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360 km/s; moment 0 detection threshold = 5 (median absolute deviation noise); min spatial size = 3''; min width = 2 channels; merging radius = 4'' and 3 channels
assumptions: Point-like continuum source at continuum map centroid; negative features in inverted cubes are purely spurious.

recipe.goal: Test significance and physical origin (kSZE) of > 4 sigma negative continuum peaks
recipe.method: Remove bright positive sources in uv-space (cl, ft, uvsub) and re-image; shift phase centre to negative peaks and fit visibilities with uv-multifit; run N=2000 visibility bootstrap simulations; evaluate analytical kSZE equations for gas mass, density, and velocity.
key_parameters: N_iter = 2000 bootstrap iterations; T_CMB = 2.7255 K; I_0 = 270.06 MJy/sr; mu_e = 1.17; cloud size <= 5'' (~30 kpc) or 1'' (5.8 kpc) for ap5
assumptions: kSZE is the sole contributor to the 233 GHz decrement (tSZE negligible at 233 GHz); no relativistic corrections required.

recipe.goal: Derive molecular gas masses from dust continuum and CO(5-4) line luminosities
recipe.method: Convert synchrotron-corrected 1.3 mm continuum fluxes to M_H2 using the Scoville et al. (2016) relation; convert CO(5-4) line luminosities of sources 20 and 32 to M_H2 using assumed CO excitation ratios and alpha_CO.
key_parameters: Continuum method: alpha_CO = 6.5 M_sun/(K km s^-1 pc^2), T_dust = 25-35 K; CO line method: L'_{J=5-4}/L'_{J=1-0} = 0.3-0.7, alpha_CO = 0.5-1 M_sun/(K km s^-1 pc^2)
assumptions: Scoville et al. (2016) empirical dust-to-gas relation holds after subtracting synchrotron flux; quasar average CO(5-4)/CO(1-0) excitation ratio applies to sources 20 and 32.

answer_key.quantity: LRS criterion high-redshift (z > 0.8) selection rate

evidence.quote: The criterion providing the highest selection rate of high-redshift sources (86% at $z>0.8$) is one combining an IR colour cut and radio flux cut ($S_{\rm 5.8\mu m} / S_{\rm 3.6\mu m}>1.3$ and $S_{\rm 1.4\,GHz}>1\,$mJy).

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of sample with redshift at z > 0.8

evidence.quote: We find that 77% of our sample with redshift measurements lie in the earliest half of cosmic history ($z>0.8$; see Tab. [\[tab:samp\]](#tab:samp)).

answer_key.quantity: Number of central mm continuum detections out of 36 candidates

evidence.quote: Among the sample of 36 sources, 16 show a millimetre (mm) detection.
11 (five) out of 36 central sources were detected at $>4.2\sigma$ ($3-4.2\sigma$) in the ACA maps, that reach a typical noise level of 0.15\,mJy.

answer_key.quantity: Number of central mm detections of non-thermal origin

evidence.quote: Among the sample of 36 sources, 16 show a millimetre (mm) detection. In eight of these cases, the emission has a non-thermal origin.
Out of the 16 central detections, 8 are of non-thermal origin (Sec. [2.2](#sec:radphot), Tab. [3](#tab:radiosed)), leaving only 8 where ACA is detecting the dust emission from the host galaxy.

answer_key.quantity: Stacked 1.3 mm continuum flux of 11 undetected sources at z > 0.8

evidence.quote: The 11 sources complying with these cuts yield a stacked signal of $0.16\pm0.05\,$mJy (3.5$\sigma$, Fig. [6](#fig:stack))

answer_key.quantity: Stacked 3 sigma upper limit for 3 undetected sources at z > 2

evidence.quote: Out of the 8 sources at $z>2$, the 3 undetected ones yield a $3\sigma$ upper-limit of 0.28\,mJy, when stacked.

answer_key.quantity: Source 9a 233 GHz continuum peak and integrated flux
Source 20a 233 GHz continuum peak and integrated flux
Source 32a 233 GHz continuum peak and integrated flux
Source 20 CO(5-4) velocity-integrated flux

evidence.quote: Source 20: the line detected at 224.156$\pm$0.003\,GHz is the brightest of the lines found serendipitously, with a velocity-integrated flux of 3.7$\pm$0.4 Jy km/s and peaking at 9$\pm$2\,mJy (FWHM=380$\pm$10\,km/s).

answer_key.quantity: Source 20 CO(5-4) line luminosity L'

evidence.quote: The measured fluxes imply line luminosities of (1.9$\pm$0.2) and (0.7$\pm$0.2)\,$\times10^{10}$ K.km/s.pc$^2$ for sources 20 and 32, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Source 20 molecular gas mass from CO(5-4)

evidence.quote: we should expect molecular gas masses in the range of 1.4–6.5 and $0.5-2.4~\times10^{10}$\,M$_\odot$ for sources 20 and 32, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Source 21 CS(6-5) velocity-integrated flux

evidence.quote: This galaxy’s spectroscopic redshift at 0.225 implies that the feature detected at 239.972$\pm$0.005\,GHz corresponds to the CS(6-5) transition ($\nu_{\rm RF}=293.912\,$GHz, $z_{\rm spec}=0.22478\pm0.00003$) with a velocity-integrated flux of 1.6$\pm$0.4 Jy km/s and peaking at 4$\pm$2\,mJy (FWHM=460$\pm$40\,km/s).

answer_key.quantity: Source 21 CS(6-5) spatial extent

evidence.quote: The morphology indicates that the emission extends about 20\,kpc out of the galaxy

answer_key.quantity: Source 32 CO(5-4) velocity-integrated flux

evidence.quote: Given the redshift of the source at $z_{\rm spec}=1.58049$, the line detected at 223.490$\pm$0.005\,GHz corresponds to the CO(5-4) transition ($\nu_{\rm RF}=576.268\,$GHz, $z_{\rm spec}=1.57850\pm0.00006$) with a velocity-integrated flux of 1.4$\pm$0.4 Jy km/s and peaking at 3$\pm$1\,mJy (FWHM=460$\pm$30\,km/s).

answer_key.quantity: Source 32 spatial offset between CO(5-4) centroid and mm continuum

evidence.quote: We note that there is a significant offset between the centroid of the line and the continuum (1.5$\pm$0.8 arcsec), with the former being more aligned with the IR detection.

answer_key.quantity: Source 32 CO(5-4) line luminosity L'

evidence.quote: The measured fluxes imply line luminosities of (1.9$\pm$0.2) and (0.7$\pm$0.2)\,$\times10^{10}$ K.km/s.pc$^2$ for sources 20 and 32, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Source 32 molecular gas mass from CO(5-4)

evidence.quote: we should expect molecular gas masses in the range of 1.4–6.5 and $0.5-2.4~\times10^{10}$\,M$_\odot$ for sources 20 and 32, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Average molecular gas mass M_H2 from dust continuum for 9 detected sources

evidence.quote: we find an average M$_{\rm H_2}=1.5-1.7\times10^{11} \,M_\odot$ for the nine detected sources with a redshift estimate (see Tabs. [\[tab:samp\]](#tab:samp) and [3](#tab:radiosed)).

answer_key.quantity: Negative peak uv-multifit fluxes (sources 20, 34, 36, ap5)

evidence.loc: The significance of the negative peaks
evidence.quote: For sources 34 and ap5, the estimated fluxes range from $-0.8$ to $-1.1$\,mJy depending on whether we leave the upper flux bound free or limited to zero, respectively. Note that source 34 was also fit assuming an axisymmetric Gaussian morphology. This yields a flux of $-0.9\pm0.2$\,mJy and a size of 5$''$$\pm$4$''$

evidence.loc: The significance of the negative peaks
evidence.quote: For the case of 20 and 36 where (positive) sources are found in the field, we fit all sources at once, and the negative peaks are found to have $-0.7$ and $-0.6$\,mJy, respectively. The uncertainties in these flux estimates are about 0.2\,mJy

answer_key.quantity: Source ap3 HNC(3-2) and HOC+(3-2) velocity-integrated fluxes

evidence.quote: The more significant one, and equally identified in the 4-channel smoothed cube, is found at 242.297$\pm$0.004\,GHz with a velocity-integrated flux of 0.4$\pm$0.1 Jy.km/s and peaking at 5$\pm$2\,mJy.
The less significant line-emission is found at 239.184$\pm$0.005\,GHz with a velocity-integrated flux of 0.5$\pm$0.2 Jy.km/s and peaking at 5$\pm$2\,mJy.

score_reason: Raw ACA data are public (2018.A.00046.S), pipeline version is exact, key imaging parameters (robust=1.5, pixel size=1'', beam, channel widths) and SoFiA parameters are thoroughly documented, and all multi-wavelength photometry and coordinates (including OT pointing offsets) are tabulated in the paper. Minor deductions for unstated tclean stopping/masking criteria, unstated cosmology, and unshared bootstrap scripts.
rediscovery_reason: Public ACA dataset of 42 pointings with clear, quantitative answer keys (continuum fluxes via imfit, radio SED power-law slopes and 233 GHz extrapolations, and serendipitous line fluxes via SoFiA) and well-specified pipeline/imaging/source-finding parameters.
